strongest_argument: Every input to this claim was published on 2026-05-26 in So-Young's own Q1 release and repeated by the CEO on the public call three months before this print - the 54 total, the 11-centre 0-3 month cohort, and the company's own framing 'a net addition of five centers during the quarter'. The word 'net' is management's, not the analyst's, and it is the same word used for Q4 ('a net addition of 10 centers'). More damagingly, the derivation is arithmetically wrong. The cohort buckets are keyed to OPERATING DURATION, and the footnote says explicitly that periods of temporary closure are excluded from that calculation and that relocated or merged centres inherit the predecessor's start date - so centres do not leave the ramp bucket on a calendar clock. Run the migration properly: mature 17 to 20 (+3 graduating from growth), growth 19 - 3 + X = 23 so X = 7 of the 13 December-cohort centres moved up, leaving 6 still inside the 0-3 bucket, and ramp = 6 carryovers + 5 genuinely new = 11, giving net +5 and a total of 54 with ZERO closures. The average-age datum decides it: 6 carryovers at ~3.1 months plus 5 new at ~0.9 months averages 2.10, matching the reported 2.1 exactly, whereas 11 fresh openings spread across Q1 would average ~1.5 and would require all eleven to be crammed into the first four weeks of January - the inverse of the quarter-end back-loading visible in Q3 (10 centres, avg age 1.0) and Q4 (13 centres, avg age 1.2). The identical model applied to Q3-to-Q4 yields 3 carryovers, 10 new, net +10, reproducing management's stated Q4 figure. The claim's 'accelerating attrition' is the boundary artefact of a company that opens stores in December.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Discloses 54 centres at 2026-03-31 with the cohort table (ramp-up 11 / 2.1 months, growth 23 / 8.0, maturity 20 / 19.8) and the footnote that phase is measured by operating duration excluding temporary-closure periods, with relocated or merged centres dated from the predecessor's commencement - both inputs to the claim and the definition that voids it.

CEO on the record: 'As of March 31, we operated 54 So-Young clinics across 16 major cities, reflecting a net addition of five centers during the quarter' and 'as of today... 59 centers in total' - the gross-versus-net distinction the claim treats as hidden is the company's own framing.
49 centres at 2025-12-31 with a ramp-up cohort of 13 at average age 1.2 months - the December-heavy opening cohort that mechanically carries six centres into the Q1 ramp bucket.
Management described Q4 2025 as 'a net addition of 10 centers during the quarter' to reach 49 - the figure the carryover model reproduces with zero closures.

baseline_evidence: The tape gives no support to a shrinking-network read: SY is +30.4% over 20 days into the print at $2.40, and the 46% distance from the 52-week high is an old de-rating - the offline-margin critique was in print by March - not a recent break. Options are non-evidence in both directions: 200 total contracts, put/call OI 0.11, no computable 25d skew, ATM spread 40% of mid. So I am not resting on the price. I am resting on publication three months before the print and on the derivation being wrong.
materiality: immaterial - even granting the claim, the six missing centres sit inside the December ramp cohort, the lowest-revenue tier at RMB2.086m per centre per quarter, so ~RMB12.6m, which is 4.1% of the RMB307-317m Q2 guide and 2.9% of Q1 total revenue of RMB432.8m; and the network was already publicly at 59 as of late May
what_would_change_my_verdict: A Q2 2026 cohort table whose ramp bucket cannot be reconciled by boundary carryover - a ramp cohort whose average age is at or below the uniform-opening expectation of ~1.5 months while the total still falls short of prior total plus ramp count - or a Chinese business-registry record of specific So-Young clinic locations deregistered in Q1 2026.
